reason: E1 and E2 support that high configurational entropy can stabilize solid-solution phases in bulk HEAs, but neither addresses nanoparticles or the full 473–1923 K range. E3 shows thermal stability of HEA nanoparticles only up to 1000 K, not 1923 K, and does not isolate configurational entropy as the cause. The key premise that entropy alone maintains stability across the entire range is thus only partly supported.
premises: High configurational entropy reduces free energy of solid-solution phases, especially at high temperatures
High configurational entropy stabilizes solid-solution phases against intermetallics or phase segregation
HEA nanoparticles maintain structural and chemical stability across 473–1923 K due to entropy stabilization
Entropy stabilization operates in nanoparticles with five or more equimolar metals
